figure.name: Leon Trotsky
figure.role: Revolutionary theorist, Bolshevik leader, exile, and critic of Soviet bureaucratic centralization.
figure.hook: Trotsky = international revolution, Soviet opposition, and bureaucracy debate.
whyHere: Trotsky belongs here because Hot2Trotski needs the revolution road to examine bureaucracy, coercive state power, exile, and dissent inside Soviet history.
He matters because the page cannot honestly discuss socialism, communism, or revolution without separating ideals, parties, states, and what power actually does.
figure.cleanIdea: The revolution question is not only how power is won. It is also how power is organized, checked, and criticized after victory.

figure.discussionText: This is the planned debate room for Trotsky: permanent revolution, Soviet opposition, bureaucracy, exile, dissent, and what revolutionary power does after victory.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The revolutionary road turns into a dispute over bureaucracy, centralization, dissent, and whether Soviet power remained accountable.

ideas.title: Permanent Revolution
ideas.plainDefinition: Permanent revolution is Trotsky's argument that socialist revolution cannot be sealed inside one national box and must keep moving internationally.
ideas.context: In the Trotsky path, permanent revolution is both a theory of revolution and a warning against treating one state as the final answer.
ideas.whyMatters: Permanent revolution matters because it shows why revolution, nationalism, state power, and internationalism collide.

ideas.title: Bureaucracy
ideas.plainDefinition: Bureaucracy means rule through offices, files, command chains, appointments, procedures, and administrators that can drift away from public accountability.
ideas.context: In the Trotsky path, bureaucracy is the warning that a revolutionary state can become its own ruling layer.
ideas.whyMatters: Bureaucracy matters because it keeps the study guide focused on power in practice, not just ideals on paper.

ideas.title: Soviet Opposition
ideas.plainDefinition: Soviet opposition means organized criticism of Soviet leadership, centralization, bureaucracy, and limits on dissent from inside or near the revolutionary tradition.
ideas.context: In the Trotsky path, Soviet opposition is not automatically anti-socialism. It is a dispute over what revolutionary power became.
ideas.whyMatters: Soviet opposition matters because it prevents the page from treating every left-wing critique of Stalin's system as the same thing as anti-communist propaganda.
